auth.title: Authentication
highlights:
# Authentication

> Choose between API keys, hosted MCP and OAuth for calling Firecrawl

There are four ways to authenticate with Firecrawl. Each one bills the team that owns the credential and gives access to the same features, so the choice depends on who holds the credential and which interface you call.

## Which should I use?

| You are building | Use | Endpoint | Credential | How it ends |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Your own code calling the REST API for your team | API key | `https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/...` | `Authorization: Bearer fc-...` | Delete the key in API keys. |
| An MCP client you configure yourself | Hosted MCP with an API key | `https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp` | `Authorization: Bearer fc-...` header in the client config | Delete the key. |
| A connector such as ChatGPT or Claude, or an MCP client with browser sign-in | MCP OAuth | `https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp-oauth` | Handled by the client. Each connection gets its own key. | Revoke it under Connected apps in Settings. |
| An app where each user connects their own Firecrawl account | OAuth for apps | `https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/...` | `Authorization: Bearer fco_...` access token. Each connection gets its own key. | Your app revokes it, or the user revokes it under Connected apps. |

If your platform creates Firecrawl accounts for its users and pays for their usage, use Firecrawl for Platforms instead.

A few REST endpoints also work with no credential at all, so you can try Firecrawl before you have a key. See No API key (keyless).

## API key

Create a key in the dashboard and send it on every request as `Authorization: Bearer fc-YOUR-API-KEY`. The SDKs take it as `apiKey`. A key has full access to the team that owns it, so keep it on your server. See Key restrictions to limit what a key can do.

## Hosted MCP with an API key

Point your MCP client at `https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp` and add the API key as a bearer token in the client config. Setup for each client is in Add an API key.

## MCP OAuth

Point your MCP client at `https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp-oauth`. The client opens a browser, the user signs in and picks a team, and Firecrawl creates a dedicated key for that connection. The client never sees the key. The native ChatGPT and Claude connectors use this flow automatically. Tokens from this flow work only on the MCP server, not on the REST API. See MCP sign-in.

## OAuth for apps

Send the user through Firecrawl's OAuth flow with `resource=https://api.firecrawl.dev/`. Your app gets an `fco_` access token that works on the REST API in place of an API key, plus an `fcr_` refresh token.

- Each connection gets its own key. Your app never sees it, and deleting another key in the dashboard doesn't affect the connection.
- The connection is listed under Connected apps in Settings, where the user can revoke it.
- Refresh tokens rotate and work once. Reusing an old refresh token revokes the whole connection.

The full flow is in OAuth for apps.

## No API key (keyless)

These REST endpoints work without an API key:

- `/v2/scrape`, `/v2/search` and `/v2/parse` (including `/v2/parse/upload-url`)
- `/v2/scrape/{jobId}/interact`
- `/v1/scrape` and `/v1/search`
- On Firecrawl Cloud, the research, developer and government search endpoints

Every other endpoint, including crawl, map, extract, agent, batch scrape and job status, needs a key. Calling one without a key returns `401`.

To make a keyless request, leave the `Authorization` header out entirely. A header with an empty token, such as `Authorization: Bearer` with nothing after it, is rejected with `401 Unauthorized: Token missing`.

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/scrape" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"url": "https://example.com"}'

```

Keyless usage is free and limited per IP address. The limits vary with demand, and a `429` response means you've reached them. Sign up for a free API key to use every endpoint with higher limits. See Keyless (no API key) on the rate limits page.

auth.title: OAuth for apps
highlights:
# OAuth for apps

> Let users connect their own Firecrawl account to your app with OAuth instead of pasting an API key

Firecrawl runs an OAuth 2.1 authorization server. Your app sends the user to Firecrawl, the user signs in and picks a team, and your app gets an access token it can use on the Firecrawl REST API in place of an API key. Usage is billed to the team the user picked.

Each connection gets its own API key, created by Firecrawl and never shown to your app. The user can see and revoke the connection under Connected apps in Settings, and deleting another key in the dashboard doesn't affect it.

> [!NOTE]
> 
> If your platform creates Firecrawl accounts for its users and pays for their usage, use Firecrawl for Platforms instead. OAuth is for users who bring their own Firecrawl account. To compare OAuth with API keys and MCP sign-in, see Authentication.

## Overview

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Discovery | `https://www.firecrawl.dev/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` |
| Authorization endpoint | `https://www.firecrawl.dev/api/oauth/authorize` |
| Token endpoint | `https://www.firecrawl.dev/api/oauth/token` |
| Revocation endpoint | `https://www.firecrawl.dev/api/oauth/revoke` |
| Registration endpoint | `https://www.firecrawl.dev/api/oauth/register` |
| Resource (audience) | `https://api.firecrawl.dev/` |
| Grant types | `authorization_code`, `refresh_token` |
| PKCE | Required, `S256` only |
| Client authentication | `none` (public clients, no client secret) |
| Access token lifetime | 1 hour, prefix `fco_` |
| Refresh token lifetime | 90 days, prefix `fcr_`, single use |

## Scopes

| Scope | Grants |
| --- | --- |
| `firecrawl:global` | Full access to the Firecrawl REST API on the chosen team, using that team's credits. This is the default when `scope` is omitted. |
| `offline_access` | Tells the user on the consent screen that your app stays connected until they revoke it. Requires `firecrawl:global`. |

A token can do anything an API key on that team can do. Request only what you need and keep tokens on your server.

## Register your app

Your app needs a `client_id`. There are two ways to get one, and neither needs approval from Firecrawl.

> [tab] Dynamic Client Registration
> 
> Register once with RFC 7591 and store the `client_id` it returns.
> 
> ```bash theme={null}
> curl -X POST https://www.firecrawl.dev/api/oauth/register \
>   -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
>   -d '{
>     "client_name": "Acme Builder",
>     "redirect_uris": ["https://acme.example/oauth/firecrawl/callback"],
>     "grant_types": ["authorization_code", "refresh_token"],
>     "token_endpoint_auth_method": "none"
>   }'
> 
> ```
> 
> The `client_name` is what users see on the consent screen.

> [tab] Client ID Metadata Document
> 
> Host a JSON metadata document at an HTTPS URL you control and use that URL as your `client_id`. Firecrawl fetches it during authorization, so you can update your name and redirect URIs without registering again. The consent screen shows the document's host to the user.
> 
> ```json theme={null}
> {
>   "client_id": "https://acme.example/oauth/firecrawl-client.json",
>   "client_name": "Acme Builder",
>   "redirect_uris": ["https://acme.example/oauth/firecrawl/callback"],
>   "grant_types": ["authorization_code", "refresh_token"],
>   "response_types": ["code"],
>   "token_endpoint_auth_method": "none"
> }
> 
> ```

Redirect URIs must use HTTPS. `http://localhost` and other loopback addresses are allowed for local development. A redirect URI may not contain a fragment or user info, and the URI you send at authorization must match a registered one exactly.

## Authorize

Generate a PKCE `code_verifier` and its S256 `code_challenge`, then send the user's browser to the authorization endpoint.

```text
https://www.firecrawl.dev/api/oauth/authorize
  ?response_type=code
  &client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID
  &redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Facme.example%2Foauth%2Ffirecrawl%2Fcallback
  &code_challenge=CODE_CHALLENGE
  &code_challenge_method=S256
  &scope=firecrawl%3Aglobal%20offline_access
  &resource=https%3A%2F%2Fapi.firecrawl.dev%2F
  &state=RANDOM_STATE

```

| Parameter | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `response_type` | Yes | Must be `code`. |
| `client_id` | Yes | From registration, or your metadata document URL. |
| `redirect_uri` | Yes | Must match a registered redirect URI. |
| `code_challenge` | Yes | Base64url SHA-256 of the `code_verifier`. |
| `code_challenge_method` | Yes | Must be `S256`. |
| `scope` | No | Space-separated. Defaults to `firecrawl:global`. |
| `resource` | No | `https://api.firecrawl.dev/` for the REST API. This is the default. |
| `state` | Recommended | Returned unchanged. Check it on the callback. |

The user signs in if needed, chooses a team, and approves. Firecrawl then redirects to your `redirect_uri` with `code` and `state`. The code is valid for a short time and only once.

If the user cancels, Firecrawl redirects with `error=access_denied`.

## Exchange the code

```bash
curl -X POST https://www.firecrawl.dev/api/oauth/token \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
  -d grant_type=authorization_code \
  -d code=AUTHORIZATION_CODE \
  -d code_verifier=CODE_VERIFIER \
  -d client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID \
  -d redirect_uri=https://acme.example/oauth/firecrawl/callback \
  -d resource=https://api.firecrawl.dev/

```

The token endpoint accepts `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` or JSON.

```json
{
  "access_token": "fco_...",
  "token_type": "bearer",
  "expires_in": 3600,
  "refresh_token": "fcr_...",
  "scope": "firecrawl:global offline_access",
  "user_id": "...",
  "team_id": "..."
}

```

`user_id` and `team_id` identify who authorized and which team is billed. Store both tokens server-side.

## Call the API

Send the access token as a bearer token, exactly like an API key.

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/scrape \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer fco_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"url": "https://example.com"}'

```

The SDKs accept the token wherever they take an API key, for example `new Firecrawl({ apiKey: "fco_..." })`.

## Refresh

Access tokens expire after one hour. Exchange the refresh token for a new pair before or after expiry.

```bash
curl -X POST https://www.firecrawl.dev/api/oauth/token \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
  -d grant_type=refresh_token \
  -d refresh_token=fcr_... \
  -d client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID

```

The response has the same shape as the code exchange. Refresh tokens rotate: each one works once, so always store the new `refresh_token` from the response. Using a refresh token a second time is treated as a stolen token: Firecrawl revokes the whole connection, including the tokens the first refresh just returned, and the user has to connect your app again. Serialize refreshes per connection and never retry a refresh that returned `invalid_grant`.

## Revoke

Call the revocation endpoint (RFC 7009) when the user disconnects Firecrawl in your app. Send the refresh token: that revokes the whole connection, including its access token and the key behind it. Sending an access token only invalidates that access token; the refresh token keeps working and the connection stays listed in the user's Settings.

```bash
curl -X POST https://www.firecrawl.dev/api/oauth/revoke \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
  -d token=fcr_...

```

The endpoint returns `200` even when the token is unknown or already revoked. Users can also revoke your app under Connected apps in Settings. A connection also ends when the authorizing user leaves the team.

## Errors

The authorization and token endpoints return standard OAuth errors as JSON: `{"error": "...", "error_description": "..."}`.

| Error | Endpoint | Meaning | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `invalid_request` | authorize, token | A required parameter is missing or malformed, for example no `code_challenge` or an unregistered `redirect_uri`. | Fix the request. |
| `invalid_client` | authorize | The `client_id` is unknown or its metadata document can't be used. | Check registration. |
| `unsupported_response_type` | authorize | `response_type` isn't `code`. | Use `code`. |
| `invalid_scope` | authorize, token | A scope isn't supported, or `offline_access` was sent without `firecrawl:global`. | Request supported scopes. |
| `access_denied` | redirect | The user cancelled on the consent screen. | Let the user try again. |
| `invalid_grant` | token | The code or refresh token is invalid, expired, already used, or revoked; the PKCE verifier, `client_id`, `redirect_uri` or `resource` doesn't match; or the user left the team. | Send the user through authorization again. |
| `unsupported_grant_type` | token | `grant_type` isn't `authorization_code` or `refresh_token`. | Fix the request. |
| `server_error` | any | Temporary failure. | Retry with backoff. |

On the REST API, an OAuth token that is expired, revoked, or unknown gets `401` with `Unauthorized: Invalid or expired OAuth token`. Refresh once, and if that fails with `invalid_grant`, ask the user to reconnect. A `503` with `OAuth authentication is temporarily unavailable` is temporary; retry with backoff. Other errors, such as `402` for insufficient credits, are the same as with an API key.

auth.title: Introduction
highlights:
## Base URL

All requests use the following base URL:

```bash
https://api.firecrawl.dev

```

## Authentication

Requests need an `Authorization` header with your API key, except on the keyless endpoints described below:

```bash
Authorization: Bearer fc-YOUR-API-KEY

```

You can find your API key in the Firecrawl dashboard.

A few endpoints, including `/v2/scrape`, `/v2/search` and `/v2/parse`, also work without a key, with limits. To call them keyless, leave the `Authorization` header out entirely, because a header with an empty token returns `401`. See No API key (keyless) for the full list.

To let users connect their own Firecrawl account to your app instead, use OAuth for apps. Authentication compares every option.

If you are an agent without an API key, start with Get credentials. If your platform supports WorkOS ID-JAG, use `auth.md` for registration instructions.

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/scrape" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer fc-YOUR-API-KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"url": "https://example.com"}'

```

```python
from firecrawl import Firecrawl

firecrawl = Firecrawl(api_key="fc-YOUR-API-KEY")

result = firecrawl.scrape("https://example.com")

```

```js
import { Firecrawl } from 'firecrawl';

const firecrawl = new Firecrawl({ apiKey: "fc-YOUR-API-KEY" });

const result = await firecrawl.scrape('https://example.com');

```

auth.title: Firecrawl auth.md
highlights:
You are an agent. Firecrawl supports agentic registration for WorkOS ID-JAG identity assertions: discover -> register -> call API. Follow the steps in order; do not skip ahead.

Firecrawl currently supports one registration method:

- `identity_assertion` with `assertion_type: "urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id-jag"`
- `requested_credential_type: "api_key"`
- Credentials are Firecrawl API keys used as bearer tokens.

Firecrawl does not currently support anonymous registration, verified-email registration, claim flows, or `access_token` issuance through `/agent/auth`. Credential revocation is supported but provider-driven (initiated by WorkOS); agents never call it — see Revocation below.

auth.title: Get Started

highlights:
#### MCP OAuth (Bearer access tokens)

Firecrawl issues OAuth **access tokens** (`fco_…`) via the authorization server on firecrawl.dev. This MCP server forwards whichever credential it resolves to the Firecrawl API as `Authorization: Bearer …`.

- **HTTP stream transports** (`CLOUD_SERVICE=true`, `HTTP_STREAMABLE_SERVER=true`, or `SSE_LOCAL=true`): Clients should send `Authorization: Bearer <fco_access_token>` on MCP requests. An OAuth bearer token takes precedence over `x-firecrawl-api-key` / `x-api-key` when both are present.
- **stdio:** Use `FIRECRAWL_OAUTH_TOKEN` for a static access token, or keep using `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY` for an API key.

Use **access** tokens (`fco_…`) only. Refresh tokens (`fcr_…`) must be exchanged at the token endpoint, not passed to the scrape/search API.

gate.title: Firecrawl for Platforms
highlights:
## Overview

Firecrawl for Platforms lets your platform create and manage Firecrawl API keys for your users directly from your own backend. Your users can then search, scrape, and interact with the web through Firecrawl, the context API for AI agents, without leaving your platform.

> [!NOTE]
> 
> Set up Firecrawl for Platforms yourself in the Firecrawl dashboard. Any admin or member of an organization can create an integration: name it, choose an integration type, accept the agreement for that type, and copy the platform key. The key is shown once. You can mint and revoke keys later under Settings. No application or approval is needed.

There are two integration types. Both provision accounts the same way through the endpoints below, with the same platform key; they differ in who pays for the user's usage:

- Standard: your users pay Firecrawl. Each provisioned account keeps its own Firecrawl plan and billing and upgrades with Firecrawl directly. See Credits for provisioned accounts for what a new account starts with.
- Gateway: your organization funds your users. Accounts your integration creates are enrolled in Gateway, so their eligible usage bills to your organization. See Gateway below.

You choose the integration type when you create the integration. It is not easy to change afterwards, so we recommend reviewing both options carefully before you accept the agreement. See the Firecrawl for Platforms page for an overview.

Some partner offers include promotional credits for provisioned users; when they do, Partner Credits describes what the user receives.

...

## Before you are verified

You can create an integration and provision accounts right away, with no application, so you can build and test your integration today. Until Firecrawl verifies your platform:

- Volume is limited. The number of accounts your integration can create is limited. That is enough to build and test, not to roll out to all your users.
- Accounts carry no free credits. See Credits for provisioned accounts.

Every `POST /partner/v1/accounts` response carries a `notice` with the code `partner_unverified` while your platform is unverified, and the Firecrawl for Platforms page in the dashboard shows the same status.

### Request verification

Add a card to your organization on the Firecrawl for Platforms page in the dashboard to verify your integration. Verification is automatic once the card is on file, and a card can verify only one organization. For a signed agreement or higher volume, write to partnerships@firecrawl.dev with your integration ID and the volume you expect.

### What verification unlocks

- Account limits that fit the volume you expect.
- The Free plan's monthly credits on new and existing accounts. For Gateway accounts those are used before your organization is billed.

...

## Credits for provisioned accounts

Accounts your integration creates do not carry free credits unless Firecrawl has verified your platform or you have a signed agreement with Firecrawl. Until then:

- A Standard account starts without included credits. The user can add a payment method or pick a plan in the Firecrawl dashboard at any time.
- A Gateway account bills every credit to your organization.

Once your platform is verified, new and existing accounts carry the Free plan's monthly credits; for Gateway accounts those are used before your organization is billed. See Request verification.

When a Gateway account runs out of credits, its requests to the Firecrawl API return `402` with the code `platform_managed_credits` and a message that tells your user to contact your platform.

...

## Partner program

Platforms that provision Firecrawl accounts for their users can apply to the Firecrawl Partner Program. Approved partners get a revenue share on paid usage from the users they bring, co-marketing and a listing in our partner directory, early access to new endpoints, a direct line to our team for technical support, and higher limits for their users. Apply and we email you next steps right away: create your integration in the dashboard and add a card to verify it.

In return, partners display "Powered by Firecrawl" in their product, linking to firecrawl.dev with their `?ref=` tag.

Rev share applies only to new paying customers you refer after your application is approved, never retroactively. Every partner is reviewed and approved by our team.

gate.title: Partner Credits
highlights:
## Overview

Firecrawl partners with select platforms to offer their users free Firecrawl credits. If you received Firecrawl credits through a partner platform, this page explains what's included and how the credits work.

## What You Get

The standard partner offer may include 10,000 free Firecrawl credits. These credits let you use any Firecrawl endpoint, including Search, Scrape, Crawl, Map, Interact, and more. See Billing for how credits are consumed per endpoint.

## Credit Expiration

Partner credits expire 3 months after they are applied to your account. Unused credits are not refunded or extended after the expiration window.

## Plan Limits

Partner credits use Firecrawl's standard Free Plan limits unless otherwise stated by the partner offer. This includes the same rate limits and concurrent browser limits as the Free plan. See Rate Limits for the full breakdown of per-plan limits.

## What's Not Included

The partner offer does not include a paid Firecrawl plan or a Hobby Plan upgrade. Your account remains on the Free plan with the associated rate limits and concurrency; you simply receive additional credits to use within that plan.

## Need More?

If you need more credits, higher rate limits, or access to paid-plan features, you can upgrade your Firecrawl account independently at any time:

- Visit the Firecrawl pricing page to compare plans
- Upgrade directly from your dashboard
- See Billing for details on available plans and Pay-as-you-go

Upgrading your plan is separate from the partner offer. Your partner credits will continue to be available alongside your plan's monthly credit allotment until they expire.

gate.title: Firecrawl for Platforms
highlights:
## Two Integration Types, One API

Both types provision accounts the same way, through the same endpoints. They differ in who pays for what your users do.

### Standard

Your users pay Firecrawl. Each account keeps its own Firecrawl plan and billing.

- Your backend calls the Platforms API and Firecrawl creates an account and API key for the user.
- Each user upgrades with Firecrawl directly, never through you. Once Firecrawl verifies your platform, accounts carry the Free plan's monthly credits.
- You are never in the billing relationship.

Best for products that let users connect their own Firecrawl.

### Gateway

Your organization funds your users' eligible usage from its own billing.

- Accounts your integration creates are enrolled in Gateway, so their eligible usage bills to your organization.
- A user's own credits are used first. Anything beyond that is billed to you.
- You keep one funding relationship with Firecrawl instead of asking each user to pay.

Best for products where Firecrawl is a built-in capability you pay for.

You choose the integration type when you create the integration and accept the agreement for that type. This choice is not easy to change afterwards, so please review both options carefully before proceeding.

## Partner Program: Revenue Share for Approved Partners

Building on Firecrawl for Platforms? Approved partners share in the revenue from the new paying customers they bring. The program is by application, and our team reviews every partner.

What approved partners get:

- Revenue share: a share of paid usage from the users you bring.
- Co-marketing: joint launches and a listing in our partner directory.
- Early access: try new endpoints before they ship.
- A direct line to our team: technical support from the people who build Firecrawl.
- Higher limits: more headroom for the users you provision.

What we ask in return: display "Powered by Firecrawl" in your product, linking to firecrawl.dev with your `?ref=<partner>` tag.

Rev share applies only to new paying customers you refer after your application is approved, never retroactively.

Apply to the Partner Program

## How It Works

No application and no waiting. Any admin or member of an organization on Firecrawl can set this up.

1. Sign in to the Firecrawl dashboard, or create an account, and open the Firecrawl for Platforms page. If you are signed out, sign-in brings you straight back to it.
2. Name your integration and choose its type: Standard, where your users pay Firecrawl, or Gateway, where your organization funds their eligible usage.
3. ... Firecra

...

4. ... It is shown once, so store it in your backend's secrets.
5. In your product, show each user Firecrawl's Terms of Service and acceptable use policy and get their acceptance. Then call the Platforms API from your server to create their account and API key.
6. Start testing right away. Until Firecrawl verifies your platform, the number of accounts you can create is limited, so when you are ready to launch, request verification.

...

Do I need to apply or be approved? No. Any admin or member of an organization on Firecrawl can create an integration from the dashboard. Sign in, choose an integration type, accept the agreement, and your key is ready. Only the Partner Program, which adds revenue share for approved partners, takes an application.

gate.title: Rate Limits
highlights:
### Keyless (no API key)

The hosted Firecrawl MCP keyless endpoint exposes exactly Search, Scrape, and Parse without an API key. Other hosted MCP tools require an account connection or an API key.

For official Firecrawl clients, the CLI, SDKs, and REST API, keyless access also includes Interact. On Firecrawl Cloud, research, developer, and government search endpoints can also be used without an API key. No other endpoints (crawl, extract, map, batch scrape, etc.) are available without a key.

Keyless usage is free and capped per IP address per day by two limits, and exceeding either returns a `429`:

- A maximum number of requests per day.
- A maximum number of credits per day. Operations cost different amounts of credits (for example, Interact and JSON extraction cost more than a basic scrape), so heavier usage reaches the credit cap sooner.

Sign up for a free API key to get 1,000 credits and higher rate limits at no cost — official clients automatically use your key once it's configured.

...

### Browser Sandbox

The browser sandbox endpoints have per-plan rate limits that scale with your subscription:

| Plan | /interact | /interact/\{id}/execute |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Free | 2 | 10 |
| Hobby | 20 | 100 |
| Standard | 100 | 500 |
| Growth | 1,000 | 5,000 |
| Scale | 1,500 | 7,500 |

In addition, each team's plan determines how many browser sessions can be active simultaneously (see Concurrent Browser Limits above). If you exceed this limit, new session requests will return a `429` status code until existing sessions are destroyed.

gate.title: Authentication
highlights:
# Authentication

> Choose between API keys, hosted MCP and OAuth for calling Firecrawl

There are four ways to authenticate with Firecrawl. Each one bills the team that owns the credential and gives access to the same features, so the choice depends on who holds the credential and which interface you call.

## Which should I use?

| You are building | Use | Endpoint | Credential | How it ends |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Your own code calling the REST API for your team | API key | `https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/...` | `Authorization: Bearer fc-...` | Delete the key in API keys. |
| An MCP client you configure yourself | Hosted MCP with an API key | `https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp` | `Authorization: Bearer fc-...` header in the client config | Delete the key. |
| A connector such as ChatGPT or Claude, or an MCP client with browser sign-in | MCP OAuth | `https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp-oauth` | Handled by the client. Each connection gets its own key. | Revoke it under Connected apps in Settings. |
| An app where each user connects their own Firecrawl account | OAuth for apps | `https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/...` | `Authorization: Bearer fco_...` access token. Each connection gets its own key. | Your app revokes it, or the user revokes it under Connected apps. |

If your platform creates Firecrawl accounts for its users and pays for their usage, use Firecrawl for Platforms instead.

A few REST endpoints also work with no credential at all, so you can try Firecrawl before you have a key. See No API key (keyless).

## API key

Create a key in the dashboard and send it on every request as `Authorization: Bearer fc-YOUR-API-KEY`. The SDKs take it as `apiKey`. A key has full access to the team that owns it, so keep it on your server. See Key restrictions to limit what a key can do.

...

## No API key (keyless)

These REST endpoints work without an API key:

- `/v2/scrape`, `/v2/search` and `/v2/parse` (including `/v2/parse/upload-url`)
- `/v2/scrape/{jobId}/interact`
- `/v1/scrape` and `/v1/search`
- On Firecrawl Cloud, the research, developer and government search endpoints

Every other endpoint, including crawl, map, extract, agent, batch scrape and job status, needs a key. Calling one without a key returns `401`.

To make a keyless request, leave the `Authorization` header out entirely. A header with an empty token, such as `Authorization: Bearer` with nothing after it, is rejected with `401 Unauthorized: Token missing`.

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/scrape" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"url": "https://example.com"}'

```

Keyless usage is free and limited per IP address. The limits vary with demand, and a `429` response means you've reached them. Sign up for a free API key to use every endpoint with higher limits. See Keyless (no API key) on the rate limits page.

Official Firecrawl MCP server, the context API for AI agents: search, scrape, and interact with the web, plus parse, crawl, map, Agent and Monitor, from any MCP client.

...

# Firecrawl MCP Server

A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that brings Firecrawl, the context API for AI agents, to MCP-compatible clients: search, scrape, and interact with the live web and get back clean Markdown or structured data.

> Big thanks to @vrknetha, @knacklabs for the initial implementation!

## Features

- Search the web, optionally with full page content for each result
- Search indexes for developer sources (GitHub issues, merged pull requests, READMEs, and docs), US government sources, and scientific papers (PubMed, bioRxiv, medRxiv, arXiv)
- Look up a protein's curated subcellular location and function in UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot, with the evidence and papers behind each statement
- Scrape any URL into clean Markdown
- Parse PDFs and documents
- Crawl a site for content from many pages, or map it to discover its URLs
- Interact with pages in a real browser: click, type, fill forms, and navigate dynamic pages
- Run Agent jobs for multi-source research that returns structured data
- Monitor pages and get notified when their content changes
- Check current and historical Firecrawl credit usage
- Automatic retries and rate limiting
- Cloud and self-hosted support
- SSE support

> Play around with our MCP Server on MCP.so's playground or on Klavis AI.

## When to Use This Server

- Use `firecrawl_scrape` when you have a known URL and want its content as markdown, then extract the requested fields yourself.
- Use `firecrawl_map` when you need to discover URLs on a site without fetching their content.
- Use `firecrawl_crawl` when you need content from many pages under a site; set `limit`, `includePaths`/`excludePaths`, or `maxDiscoveryDepth` to bound it.
- Use `firecrawl_search` when you're starting from a query rather than a URL and want ranked web results. Results carry excerpts; fetch full pages with `firecrawl_scrape` on the URLs you need. `scrapeOptions` fetches every result's page in the same call and bills each as a scrape, so keep it for the full text of a few results (the search-only endpoint never fetches content).
- Use `firecrawl_interact` when a page needs a click, type, or navigate action before you can read it: pass a `url` for a fresh page or a `scrapeId` to continue on one you already scraped.
- Use the `firecrawl_monitor_*` tools when the same page needs to be checked on a recurring schedule with diffs and change alerts, rather than fetched once.
- Use `firecrawl_credit_usage` to check credits left or what credits were spent on, by month or day, optionally broken down by endpoint or API key.
- Consider something else when you need to hold a browser session open across many of your own steps with your own retry and termination logic: each `firecrawl_interact` call runs one `prompt` or `code` turn to completion and returns control. The session can persist across calls via `scrapeId` and ends with `firecrawl_interact_stop`, but you cannot drive it interactively step-by-step from the client side within a single call.

This server lists 34 tools when the full profile registers with default settings (feedback tools included, not running in local-keyless mode). Setting `FIRECRAWL_NO_SEARCH_FEEDBACK=1` and/or `FIRECRAWL_NO_ENDPOINT_FEEDBACK=1` removes the corresponding feedback tools and reduces this count, as does local keyless startup. For clients with a tool-slot limit: the hosted keyless endpoint (`https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp`, no API key) exposes only 3 (`firecrawl_scrape`, `firecrawl_search`, `firecrawl_parse`), and the dedicated search-only endpoint (`https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp-search`) exposes a fixed set of 12 tools (search, developer, government, and research search, Alexandria catalogue lookup and execution, people and company search and enrichment, and job postings).

## Installation

### Hosted MCP (keyless free tier)

Connect to the remote hosted server with no setup:

```
https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp
```

On the keyless free tier, `scrape`, `search`, and `parse` work without an API key (rate-limited). Other tools such as `crawl`, `map`, and `agent` still need a key.

Prefer OAuth or an API key whenever the human can sign up. It unlocks the full tool set and higher limits.

For an interactive account connection, configure your MCP client to use this server URL. This is an MCP endpoint, **not a browser page**; use the client's account-connection flow and do not add a second Firecrawl server entry when reconnecting:

```
https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp-oauth
```

For an API-key connection (for example, an unattended integration), keep the server URL as:

```
https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp
```

Then configure the client's secure header or secret setting with:

```
Authorization: Bearer <FIRECRAWL_API_KEY>
```

Never put an API key in the server URL. Never put an API key in an agent chat. Configure it directly in the client or secret manager. See the hosted MCP setup guide and the agent onboarding guide for client-specific instructions.

...

#### Search-only endpoint

A fixed-scope search surface is also hosted at:

```
https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp-search
```

It exposes a fixed set of twelve tools: `firecrawl_search`, `firecrawl_developer_search`, `firecrawl_gov_search`, the four `firecrawl_research_*` paper tools, the two Alexandria tools `firecrawl_find_tools` and `firecrawl_scrape`, and the enrich tools `people_company_search` and `people_company_enrich`, and the jobs tool `jobs_search`. Its `firecrawl_search` fetches no page content.

highlights:
# Get Started

> Set up Firecrawl MCP with keyless access, account sign-in, or an API key.

Choose how the connection will authenticate. Signing in and adding an API key are two paths to the same access: both reach the full tool surface on your team's plan.

> [card] Try Instantly
> 
> No account or key. Search, Scrape, and Parse within daily limits.

> [card] Sign in
> 
> Browser sign-in from Codex, Claude Code, or your favorite harness.

> [card] Use an API key
> 
> Configure an API key in your client, no browser needed.

...

## Sign in

Point your client at the OAuth server URL. Your client opens a browser window where you sign in to Firecrawl and approve a team:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "firecrawl": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp-oauth"
    }
  }
}

```

No API key or headers are needed. Review and revoke connections from MCP settings.

> [!NOTE]
> 
> This is a server URL for your MCP client, not a page to open directly in a browser. API-key connections use `https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp` with a bearer token instead; see Add an API key.

mcp.title: Firecrawl MCP tools
highlights:
# Firecrawl MCP tools

> Choose a Firecrawl MCP tool and understand its availability and operating behavior.

Firecrawl MCP exposes tools for finding, extracting, interacting with, and monitoring web content. Your MCP client receives the exact input schema for every available tool when it connects.

## Tool availability

| Connection mode | Available tools |
| --- | --- |
| Hosted OAuth | Full tool surface, subject to plan and team policy |
| Hosted API key | Full tool surface, subject to plan and team policy |
| Hosted keyless | `firecrawl_search`, `firecrawl_scrape`, and `firecrawl_parse` |
| Local with the Firecrawl cloud API | API-backed tools; direct local-file Parse is unavailable |
| Local with a self-hosted Firecrawl API | Tools supported by the services enabled in that deployment |

Start with Get Started and pick For Agents or For Humans. Some optional tools can be disabled by environment or team policy.

## Choose a tool

| Job | Tool | Use it when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Read one page | `firecrawl_scrape` | You know the URL and need page content or structured fields. |
| Get fields from a known page | `firecrawl_scrape` with `formats: ["markdown"]` | You have the URL and want specific fields. Extract them from the returned content, or use `firecrawl_agent` when the pages are not known. |
| Discover site URLs | `firecrawl_map` | You need to find pages before deciding what to extract. |
| Search the web | `firecrawl_search` | You have a query rather than a known URL. |
| Get data from a third-party provider | `alexandria_library_search`, then `alexandria_library_read` | You need typed records from a provider in the Alexandria catalogue. Authenticated `firecrawl_search` also returns matching tools in `data.tools`. |
| Save a team skill | `firecrawl_save_skill` | You want to create or change one of your team's skills in the Alexandria library, written out or copied from a library skill. |
| Find people or companies | `people_company_search` | You need a list of people by title, seniority, function, employer, or location, or companies by industry, headcount, location, technology, or founding year. |
| Enrich known people or companies | `people_company_enrich` | You have names, domains, LinkedIn URLs, emails, or phone numbers and need profiles, firmographics, work or personal email, or mobile. |
| Find job postings | `jobs_search` | You need postings by role and place, a company's open roles from its own job board, who is hiring for a role, or whether up to 10 posting URLs are still open. |
| Parse a file | `firecrawl_parse` | You need content from a PDF, document, spreadsheet, or HTML file. |
| Extract many pages | `firecrawl_crawl` and `firecrawl_check_crawl_status` | You need to traverse a site or section. The crawl tool polls the job to a terminal state before returning. |
| Run autonomous research | `firecrawl_agent` and `firecrawl_agent_status` | The task spans multiple sources and the exact pages are not known. |
| Operate a live page | `firecrawl_interact` and `firecrawl_interact_stop` | You need clicks, form fills, navigation, or dynamic-page extraction. |
| Search scientific literature | `firecrawl_research_search_papers`, `firecrawl_research_inspect_paper`, `firecrawl_research_read_paper`, and `firecrawl_research_related_papers` | You need to find papers, read passages from inside one, or follow citations. Searches the Research Index of PubMed, bioRxiv, medRxiv, and arXiv paper abstracts. |
| Look up a protein | `firecrawl_research_lookup_protein` | You have one protein in mind and need its subcellular location or function, with the evidence kind for each statement and the papers UniProt cites. Pass a UniProt accession, or a gene symbol with an organism. See Look up a protein. |
| Answer a programming question | `firecrawl_developer_search` | You need primary-source answers from issues, merged pull requests, READMEs, and curated docs. |
| Answer a legal or regulatory question | `firecrawl_gov_search` | You need statutes, regulations, codes, court opinions, or other government publications from the Firecrawl Government Index. |
| Monitor changes | `firecrawl_monitor_*` | You need recurring checks, diffs, and webhook or email notifications. |
| Check credit usage | `firecrawl_credit_usage` | You need the team's remaining credits, or what credits were spent on by month or day, optionally split by endpoint or API key. |
| Send product feedback | `firecrawl_search_feedback` and `firecrawl_feedback` | You want to rate search results or report endpoint-level quality. |

`firecrawl_gov_search` also accepts the optional filters `jurisdiction`, `court`, `courtType`, `cites`, and `domain` (`firecrawl-mcp` 3.34.0 or later). See Government Index filters.

`jobs_search`, `firecrawl_save_skill`, and `firecrawl_research_lookup_protein` are on the hosted server. The local `firecrawl-mcp` 3.40.0 release does not include them yet.

> [!NOTE]
> 
> The former Extract MCP tool is deprecated and is not part of the current tool surface. Use Scrape for a known page and extract the fields from its content, or Agent when Firecrawl must discover the sources. See Choosing the Data Extractor for the full comparison.

> [!TIP]
> 
> Use the schema shown by your MCP client for the current arguments. The feature guides below explain the underlying Firecrawl behavior without duplicating those schemas here.

mcp.title: Introduction
highlights:
# Introduction

> The context API for AI agents. Search the web, scrape any page, and interact with it through one API.

Firecrawl is the context API for AI agents. Search, scrape, and interact with the live web to get clean Markdown or structured data.

## Get started

Connect over Streamable HTTP. The keyless server URL (Search, Scrape, and Parse; no credential required) is `https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp`.

- Codex CLI: `codex mcp add firecrawl --url https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp`
- Claude Code: `claude mcp add --transport http firecrawl https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp`
- Cursor or any JSON-config client: `{"mcpServers": {"firecrawl": {"url": "https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp"}}}`
- OpenCode (`opencode.json`): `{"mcp": {"firecrawl": {"type": "remote", "url": "https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp", "enabled": true}}}`
- ChatGPT or Claude.ai: use the native Firecrawl connector — ChatGPT or Claude.

Both setup paths and API-key setup: MCP Get Started, For Agents, and For Humans.

mcp.title: Firecrawl
highlights:
## MCP Server

Give any MCP client Firecrawl's tools to search the web, scrape pages, crawl and map sites, parse documents, interact with dynamic pages, run Agent, set up monitors, search research papers and the Developer Index, and call Alexandria data providers. Use the hosted server, or run it yourself.

- Keyless (Markdown): connect to `https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp` with no API key for rate-limited Search, Scrape, and Parse. Add an API key or sign in for every tool and higher limits
- Hosted server: `https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp` (API key as a Bearer token) or `https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp-oauth` (OAuth sign-in)
- Local server: `npx -y firecrawl-mcp` with `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY` set
